observations.text: SP flew Slow Flight to the level required for this block, with the IP directing the entry configuration and setting the power for the maneuver. Altitude excursions reached 300 feet and heading excursions 10 degrees before the SP acted on the IP's direction, and the recovery to level flight was not initiated independently. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the pitch, power and airspeed relationship described in the Techniques and Procedures manual is expected to become self-managed on the next exposure.

SP established and sustained Slow Flight after verbal prompts from the IP, without the IP taking the controls at any stage. Airspeed excursions reached 15 knots above the target and altitude excursions 300 feet, recognized and corrected with delay once prompted. No inadvertent stall characteristics appeared during the maneuver. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP configured, entered and recovered Slow Flight from the briefed sequence, without IP direction and without IP intervention. Minor deviations of 220 feet in altitude, 10 knots above the target airspeed and 8 degrees in heading were detected by the SP and corrected in a timely manner. No inadvertent stall characteristics were allowed to develop. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed Slow Flight in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures manual, entering, sustaining and recovering the maneuver with no prompting from the IP. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within +4/-0 knots and heading and bank within 4 degrees, with every correction applied accurately and without delay. The approach of stall characteristics was anticipated and never allowed to develop. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed Slow Flight with exceptional accuracy for this stage of training, setting the configuration, power and trim without reference to any prompt. Altitude, airspeed and heading deviations were negligible throughout, remaining within 50 feet, +2/-0 knots and 2 degrees. SP flew the maneuver above the minimum safe altitude and kept a positive stall margin at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a trim technique that did not follow the pitch change after the power reduction, did not stabilize the attitude required to sustain Slow Flight, and the airspeed decayed until the stall warning activated. The IP took the controls and recovered the aircraft to level flight. Altitude loss reached 420 feet and airspeed fell 8 knots below the target, beyond the limits of 300 feet and 5 knots.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments, did not monitor the airspeed while adjusting the power for Slow Flight and did not prevent the inadvertent appearance of stall characteristics. The IP directed the recovery and set the configuration for the second entry. Deviations reached 450 feet in altitude and 18 degrees in heading, beyond the limits of 300 feet and 10 degrees.

SP completed Slow Flight within the standards of the block, but only after the IP's verbal prompts on the power setting and on the nose position. Altitude excursions reached 290 feet and heading excursions 10 degrees, recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the airspeed trend is expected to reduce the need for prompting on the next sortie.

SP entered and sustained Slow Flight without prompting from the IP, applying the pitch and power corrections described in the Techniques and Procedures manual. Minor deviations of 200 feet in altitude, 8 knots above the target airspeed and 7 degrees in heading were self-detected and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed Slow Flight accurately and without hesitation, establishing the configuration, power and trim in the briefed sequence. Altitude was maintained within 100 feet, airspeed within +3/-0 knots and heading and bank within 3 degrees, and the recovery was initiated at the correct point. No inadvertent stall characteristics were allowed to appear. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed Slow Flight to a standard above the desired level for this block, anticipating the pitch change at each power adjustment instead of reacting to it. Deviations were negligible throughout, within 40 feet in altitude, +2/-0 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in heading and bank. SP held the maneuver above the minimum safe altitude and stated the stall margin available at each stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an entry technique in which the power was reduced before the pitch attitude was set, did not sustain the airspeed required for Slow Flight, and the aircraft entered a descent with the stall warning activating. The IP took the controls to recover the aircraft to level flight. Altitude loss reached 500 feet and airspeed fell 10 knots below the target, beyond the limits of 300 feet and 5 knots.

SP, due to a failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased, did not maintain the scan while flying Slow Flight and did not prevent the inadvertent appearance of stall characteristics. The maneuver was not completed without assistance and the IP executed the recovery. Heading deviation reached 20 degrees and altitude deviation 380 feet, both beyond the limits of 10 degrees and 300 feet.

SP, due to an under-controlled elevator input at the point where the airspeed began to decay, did not hold the pitch attitude required for Slow Flight and did not restore the target speed until prompted by the IP. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and airspeed reached 5 knots below the target, at the limit and corrected with delay. No IP intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to an aircraft state that had diverged from the SP's mental model without being reassessed, did not identify the developing sink rate in Slow Flight and held the same power setting throughout. Only after the IP's verbal prompts did the SP add power and re-establish the maneuver. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and heading deviation 10 degrees, at the limit, recognized and corrected with delay and without IP intervention on the controls.

SP flew Slow Flight within the desired standards for the block, without prompting or intervention by the IP. Altitude twice drifted to 250 feet and heading to 9 degrees before the corrections were applied, and airspeed peaked at 12 knots above the target. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter trim and scan cycle is expected to bring the deviations closer to 150 feet and 5 degrees on the next sortie.

SP executed Slow Flight in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures manual, with an accurate and prompt entry, sustainment and recovery. Altitude was held within 110 feet, airspeed within +4/-0 knots and heading and bank within 4 degrees, with no IP prompting at any stage. Stall characteristics were never allowed to appear inadvertently. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed Slow Flight with exceptional accuracy, trimming the aircraft so that the maneuver was sustained with minimal control input. Deviations were negligible throughout, remaining within 40 feet in altitude, +2/-0 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in heading and bank. SP briefed the minimum safe altitude and the stall margin before entry and flew the profile above both. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt and excessive aileron input while correcting the heading in Slow Flight, did not keep the bank inside the limits and did not coordinate the correction, allowing the buffet to develop. The IP intervened on the controls to recover the aircraft to level flight. Bank exceeded 20 degrees and altitude loss reached 450 feet, both beyond the limits of 10 degrees and 300 feet.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised recovery sequence, did not apply the pitch and power inputs required when the stall warning activated in Slow Flight, and the maneuver was not completed without assistance. The IP took the controls, recovered the aircraft and re-entered the maneuver. Airspeed fell 12 knots below the target and altitude loss reached 600 feet, beyond the limits of 5 knots and 300 feet.

SP, due to a power setting selected without reference to the configuration actually set, did not establish the airspeed required for Slow Flight at the first attempt and did not identify the error until prompted. Airspeed stabilized at 15 knots above the target and altitude deviation reached 300 feet, both at the limit and corrected with delay. The maneuver was completed on verbal prompts alone, without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected, did not question the continuing sink in Slow Flight and did not adjust the power until the IP called for it. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and heading deviation 10 degrees, at the limit and recognized only after the prompt. The recovery to level flight was then flown by the SP without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to a trim technique that lagged the pitch change at each power adjustment, did not hold the nose position steady in Slow Flight and made repeated elevator corrections. Altitude deviation reached 230 feet and heading deviation 8 degrees, with airspeed peaking at 11 knots above the target. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner by the SP, without IP intervention.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action, did not maintain the airspeed and altitude cross-check during Slow Flight and allowed the nose to drop. The deviation reached 240 feet in altitude and 9 degrees in heading before it was detected. SP corrected both in a timely manner without any IP prompt or intervention, and no stall characteristics appeared.

SP executed Slow Flight in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures manual and within the desired standards, without IP prompting or intervention. Altitude was contained within 145 feet and heading within 5 degrees, at the edge of the tolerance, and two corrections were needed to keep the airspeed inside +5/-0 knots. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a steadier trim and a faster scan cycle are expected to consolidate the accuracy on the next sortie.

SP executed Slow Flight with exceptional accuracy and full control of the maneuver, anticipating each pitch and power change instead of correcting after it. Deviations were negligible throughout, within 30 feet in altitude, +2/-0 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in heading and bank. SP maintained the minimum safe altitude, kept a positive stall margin and stated the recovery criteria before entry. Above end of block MIF achieved.
